title: Mercator: cooperative preemption and KV backpressure shaping for latency-safe continuous batching
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: implement a cooperative preemption policy (Mercator) that reduces hard interrupts while preserving tenant SLOs under heavy KV-residency and GPU memory pressure. Mercator focuses on graceful yielding, predictive KV backpressure shaping, and selective spill-to-CPU for long-lived KV working sets. This ticket covers design, prototyping in the runner, benchmark validation, and a staged rollout behind a runtime feature flag.
design_notes: Motivation: hard preemption causes latency cliffs when multiple tenants hold large KV caches; eviction storms and batch thrashing increase p95 for latency-sensitive tenants.

Approach: replace immediate interrupt-with-evict with a cooperative two-phase yield: 1) soft-yield window where a tenant's batch voluntarily reduces batch size / pauses new admission for X ms; 2) if pressure persists, perform bounded eviction + preempt. Soft-yield decisions driven by predicted KV residency and per-tenant latency slack.

KV shaping: maintain per-tenant KV watermark (hot, warm, cold) based on access rate + residency time; when entering hot->warm threshold, Mercator throttles admission and increases batching prioritization for low-latency tenants.

GPU memory management: introduce a 'headroom estimator' that uses current KV slab usage + active batch token envelope to pre-reserve a safe margin for high-priority requests to avoid OOMs during eviction spikes.
Predictive model: lightweight EWMA of sequence length and KV hits to forecast near-term working set growth (100ms horizon). Use forecast to decide soft-yield vs immediate preempt.

Fallbacks: if KV pressure + queue depth exceed configured thresholds, fallback to existing forced preempt path to guarantee throughput and avoid starvation. This keeps backward compatibility with current runtime behavior.

API & config knobs: feature flag runtime.flag.mercator_enabled, per-tenant allowlist, soft_yield_ms (default 30), kv_hot_threshold_pct (default 0.75), headroom_margin_bytes (default 256MB), predictive_alpha (default 0.2).

Telemetry: add metrics mercator.soft_yield.count, mercator.hard_preempt.count, mercator.eviction.rate, mercator.prediction.error, per-tenant latency delta post-yield. Expose sampling traces for representative requests.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests for cooperative yield decision logic and headroom estimator exist and pass in CI.

Staging perf: under mixed workload (50% latency-sensitive, 50% batchy) measured p95 latency for latency-sensitive tenants does not regress more than 5% compared to baseline, and p50 improves by at least 2% due to fewer hard-eviction spikes.
Memory safety: no OOMs in 3h stress test with KV working set growth synthetic generator; eviction rate must be stable (no >3x spikes vs baseline).
Metrics: mercator.soft_yield.count should be >0 in stress tests and mercator.hard_preempt.count should be reduced by at least 40% vs baseline.
Rollout plan validated: feature flag gate with per-cluster opt-in, canary with 5% of traffic, observed metrics dashboard shows expected behavior before full rollout.
Docs: Operator runbook in Console runbooks with remediation steps and config example.
Performance dashboard: link to staging dashboard shows the above metrics (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/mercator-staging)

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Predictions underestimate working set growth -> late preemption -> transient OOMs. Mitigation: conservative default headroom and immediate fallback to forced preempt when GPU free < 10%.
Risk: Cooperative yield increases tail latency if misconfigured for workloads that can't tolerate pauses. Mitigation: per-tenant allowlist and small default soft_yield_ms (30ms).
Risk: Telemetry blind spots. Mitigation: sample detailed traces for first two canaries, keep aggressive alerting on mercator.prediction.error > 0.2.
Risk: Interactions with KV compaction/quantization paths. Mitigation: coordinate with model-onboarding to mark large KV consumers and consider static reservations for pinned workloads.
notes: Experiment results (internal): prototype reduced hard_preempt.count by 55% in a synthetic mix where 20% of tenants had large long-lived KV sets (report: drive link in design doc).
Observed trade-off: soft-yield windows introduced ~8ms median increase for batches that yielded, but <3% impact on end-to-end p95 for affected tenants due to fewer eviction cascades.
